name: settings
title: Settings
summary: Market-level platform settings: country and service region, currency, time zone, business hours, support contacts, guest checkout, Android app versions and feature flags, plus the effective-dated change process (impact preview, approval, schedule, apply) for every runtime setting a module declares. It also assembles the Admin Center settings page from sections owned by other modules.
owns: Market: country, service region, currency, time zone, locale
Business hours, support closures and support contact details (used for business-hour deadlines and the Help pages)
Checkout toggles: guest checkout, offer an account after a guest purchase
App configuration for the website and the Android app: support hours, feature flags, minimum and latest Android version, maintenance notice
Setting definition registry: runtime settings declared by any module (key, type, default, approval rule, minimum notice)
Effective-dated values with history: every change has an effective date, an apply scope (new orders only or open commitments), a reason and an impact preview before saving
Setting change requests: draft → approval when required → scheduled → applied, and cancellation
Feature flags for runtime switches inside enabled modules
The settings overview page: settings-owned sections plus summaries of sections owned by other modules, and all scheduled changes in one list
notOwns: Returns baseline, category exceptions and who pays return shipping: returns (versioned policy with its own approval and impact preview). settings only shows its summary and scheduled change on the page
Commission rules, fee basis, payout schedule, availability delay, minimum payout and hold rules: finance (fee rule versions, payout settings). settings shows them as a linked section
Shipping defaults (seller dispatch target, Official Store cutoff, free-delivery threshold, missing-tracking flag), carrier services and no-dispatch holidays: shipping
Advertising rules (opening-ad frequency, overlays per page, no-ad pages, labels, paid seller ads): advertising global rules
Seller performance targets: sellers; support SLA targets per case category: support
Which modules are installed at all: modules.config.ts (code). Feature flags only switch behaviour inside enabled modules
Staff roles and approval limits: access; the Business Owner approval itself is an access approval request
Policy texts shown to customers (returns policy page, purchase terms): content

publicApi.name: get
publicApi.desc: Value in force at a time (default now), falling back to the declared default. Cached; invalidated by settings.setting.changed. key is the full '<module>.<name>': any module may read another enabled module's declared setting (read-only), e.g. audit reads reports.maxExportRows; the kernel exposes it as ctx.settings.read(fullKey) next to ctx.settings.get(ownName). An unknown key or a disabled module's key throws UNKNOWN_SETTING.

publicApi.name: businessCalendar
publicApi.signature: () => { isOpen(at: datetime): bool, isBusinessDay(day: date): bool, addBusinessMinutes(from: datetime, minutes: int): datetime, addBusinessDays(from: datetime, days: int): datetime, nextOpen(after: datetime): datetime }
publicApi.desc: Business-hour arithmetic in the market time zone for SLA deadlines. addBusinessDays counts whole days that have opening hours (closures and closed weekdays skipped) and keeps the local time of day, moved to closing time when that day closes earlier; from inside a closed day it counts from the next business day.

stateMachines.name: Setting change
stateMachines.notes: submit is refused while the impact preview has blocking items (effective date inside minLeadDays, invalid value) or another open change touches the same key (CHANGE_CONFLICT). The strictest approval rule among the items applies (business_owner > second_reviewer > none); approval goes through access and finishes on access.approval.decided: action settings.changes.apply-owner (Business Owner only) when any item's rule is business_owner, otherwise settings.changes.apply (a second reviewer). A Platform Administrator can therefore never approve a Business Owner rule change. apply runs at effectiveAt (job) and writes a new version per key; a change whose effectiveAt is now applies immediately after approval. Applied changes are never edited: a correction is a new change.

SETTING_NOT_EDITABLE.meaning: The setting is read-only (e.g. currency fixed for launch) or owned by a module section that is edited there (details.link).

IMPACT_BLOCKING.meaning: The impact preview has blocking items; details.blocking lists them.

CHANGE_CONFLICT.meaning: Another open change touches the same setting (details.changeRef). Cancel it or combine them.

LEAD_TIME_TOO_SHORT.meaning: The effective date is earlier than the setting's minimum notice (details.earliest).

notes: Boundary: settings owns market-level values (market.*, support.*, checkout.*, apps.*) and the generic store for runtime settings that modules declare in their manifest (the same `settings` entries as in their specs, opted in with editable: true). Versioned business rule sets with their own lifecycle stay in their modules: returns baseline and category exceptions (returns), fee rules and payout/hold settings (finance), shipping defaults and holidays (shipping), advertising global rules (advertising), seller performance targets (sellers), SLA targets (support). Those modules register a section provider so GET /overview shows their values, last change and scheduled changes, and the page edits them through the owning module's endpoint (SectionLink).

Removed keys are dropped from the store by a settings migration (stored values and scheduled changes), as for finance's second-reviewer thresholds and promotions' referencePriceDays: the fulfillment-service key warehouseAddress was removed (the inbound destination is the service location's address, fulfillment-service.serviceLocationId).

Every change states its effective date and its impact on existing commitments before saving (plan ch. 18). applyScope new_only means orders placed before the effective date keep what they accepted; purchase snapshots in orders already guarantee this for terms copied at purchase.

Settings-owned keys and their defaults (examples to confirm): market.country = US; market.serviceRegion = 48 contiguous states (Alaska, Hawaii and territories later); market.currency = USD (not editable at launch); market.timeZone = America/Los_Angeles; market.locale = en-US; support.businessHours = Mon–Sat 08:00–20:00; support.closures = Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year; support.phone = 1-800-555-0136; checkout.guestCheckoutEnabled = true (approval: business_owner); checkout.offerAccountAfterGuestPurchase = true; market.legalName = Marketly, Inc. and market.companyLine (approval: business_owner; shown in footers, policies and emails); apps.android.minVersionCode, apps.android.latestVersionCode, apps.android.updateUrl; apps.maintenance.

Launch has one market (plan ch. 1: one service region and one main currency; no other languages are planned). AppConfig.market (United States · English (US) · USD) is still returned for formatting, but the apps show no market row and no market or language picker and no supportedMarkets list until an expansion project adds a second market.

apps.maintenance holds { active, kind, message, until }; every change sets updatedAt. kind incident is used by the Platform Administrator for live service problems so error pages can show the current status note.
Changing market.timeZone or market.currency after launch needs a migration plan: both are business_owner approval, minLeadDays 30, and currency stays read-only in phase 1 (one currency, plan ch. 1).

Feature flags never replace module enablement: a disabled module's endpoints do not exist, whatever a flag says. Public flags appear in app-config so the Android app can hide features (e.g. wishlist in phase 3).
Seller support hours share the general support business hours and closures; there is no separate seller schedule, and GET /api/seller/support/categories (hoursLabel, openNow) reads the same values.
